name: Gurugram Tech Employee Unpaid Salary & Relieving Letter Withheld
raw_input: I worked as a frontend developer at an IT consultancy firm in Cyber City, Gurugram for 18 months at Rs 70,000/month. I submitted my resignation on 1st August 2024 and completed my full 60-day notice period till 30th September 2024. All project handovers and company assets (MacBook, ID card) were handed over and I received an asset clearance certificate from IT. My August salary was delayed, and my September salary plus 15 days encashable leave (total Rs 1,65,000) has not been paid. It has been 50 days since my last working day. Whenever I email HR, they say 'finance team is facing client payment delays'. More importantly, they are withholding my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate. My new employer is threatening to cancel my job offer if I don't submit my relieving letter by end of this week. I have my appointment letter, resignation acceptance email, and signed clearance form.

case_dossier.case_title: Withholding of Final Settlement and Relieving Letter by IT Consultancy Firm
case_dossier.summary: The complainant worked as a frontend developer for 18 months, completed a 60-day notice period ending September 30, 2024, and cleared all company assets. The employer has failed to pay the August salary, September salary, and 15 days of encashable leave totaling Rs. 1,65,000, and is additionally withholding the relieving letter and experience certificate, jeopardizing the complainant's new job offer.

Complainant submitted resignation and served the 60-day notice period.
Last working day; complainant completed project handovers, returned company assets, and received an asset clearance certificate.

Salary for August, September, and 15 days encashable leave (total Rs. 1,65,000) remained unpaid, and HR delayed responding with excuses of client payment delays while withholding the Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate.

case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Strong documentary proof including appointment letter, resignation acceptance, and clearance certificate, though bank statements and formal demand notices would further solidify the claim.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
Your right to receive final settlement and relieving documents upon leaving a job is legally protected under Indian law. Under Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, 2019, your unpaid wages must be paid within two working days of your resignation or removal. This is fundamentally a civil employment dispute rather than a criminal matter, meaning you should pursue remedies through proper statutory forums rather than filing police complaints.

Key statutory rule: Section 17(2) mandates payment within two working days of leaving.
Immediate takeaway: Send a formal demand notice to your employer and prepare to approach the competent labor authority if they fail to comply.

governing_laws.relevance: Mandates that the wages of an employee who resigns must be paid within two working days of that event.
Clarifies that withholding wages or breach of employment contracts are civil disputes and not criminal offenses unless initial fraudulent intent is proven.

action_options.title: Send a Formal Demand Notice
action_options.details: Send a formal written demand email and notice to your employer citing Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, 2019, requesting the immediate release of your unpaid wages and relieving documents within two working days.

action_options.title: Approach the Competent Labor Authority
action_options.details: If the employer fails to settle your dues, approach the competent labour authority (confirm locally) for formal proceedings and recovery. Note: You can contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Helpline 15100 for free legal aid and guidance only; it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings against an employer.

action_options.title: Pursue Formal Conciliation and Adjudication
action_options.details: Participate in labor conciliation proceedings initiated through the labor authority to secure your full and final settlement and experience certificates.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: Because this involves complex employment recovery and employer pushback impacting a new job offer, consulting a licensed advocate or utilizing free legal aid through the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA / NALSA Helpline 15100) is strongly advised.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**FROM:** 
[Your Name] 
[Your Address] 
Phone: [Your Phone Number] 
Email: [Your Email Address] 

**DATE:** 09/11/2026

**MODE OF DISPATCH:** Speed Post with Acknowledgement Due (AD) / Registered Email

**TO:** 
The Management / Human Resources Department 
IT Consultancy Firm 
Cyber City, Gurugram 
[Company Email Address, if known] 

---

### **SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR RELEASE OF UNPAID SALARY, LEAVE ENCASHMENT, RELIEVING LETTER, AND EXPERIENCE CERTIFICATE TOTUMING TO RS. 1,65,000**

Dear Sir/Madam,

I, am serving this Legal Demand Notice upon you from myself as an aggrieved ex-employee, to demand the immediate settlement of my pending dues and the issuance of my statutory relieving documents.

I hereby state and submit as under:

1. That for 18 months prior to August 2024, I worked as a Frontend Developer at your IT consultancy firm located in Cyber City, Gurugram, drawing a monthly salary of Rs. 70,000.
2. That on 1st August 2024, I formally submitted my resignation and diligently served the 60-day notice period as required by my employment terms.
3. That 30th September 2024 marked my last working day, on which I successfully completed all project handovers, returned all company assets in good condition, and duly received an asset clearance certificate from your authorized representatives.
4. That post 30th September 2024 (past 50 days), my salary for August 2024, salary for September 2024, and 15 days of encashable leave—totaling an amount of Rs. 1,65,000—have remained unpaid. Furthermore, HR has delayed responding with excuses of client payment delays while wrongfully withholding my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate, thereby severely jeopardizing my new job offer.
5. That your withholding of my statutory dues and essential employment documents is in direct violation of applicable Indian employment laws, including Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, 2019, which mandates that the wages of an employee who resigns must be paid promptly.

### **DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION**

I hereby call upon you to clear my full and final settlement of **Rs. 1,65,000** and issue my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate within **15 days** of receiving this notice. 

Payment must be remitted directly to my salary bank account on record. 

### **WARNING OF LEGAL ACTION**

If you fail to comply with this demand within the stipulated 15-day rectification window, I shall be constrained to initiate formal legal proceedings against your firm before the competent labour authority (confirm locally) for the recovery of my dues and statutory compensation, without any further notice to you. 

*(Note: For free legal aid, guidance, or information regarding your rights, you may contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline at 15100).*

Sincerely / Yours faithfully,

*(Signature)* 
[Your Name] 
Frontend Developer (Ex-Employee)

---

### **ANNEXURE INVENTORY**
1. Copy of Appointment Letter
2. Copy of Resignation Acceptance Email
3. Copy of Signed Asset Clearance Form
4. Copies of Emails with HR regarding payment delays

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under employment laws, full and final dues must be cleared timely and withholding my relieving letter violates my right to livelihood. If my Rs 1,65,000 and relieving letter are not issued within 3 days, I will file a formal complaint with the District Labor Commissioner.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre, listen! Don't give me all these big threats about District Labor Commissioner and right to livelihood. Read your employment agreement—clearance pending hai, internal audits are going on, and exit formalities take time according to company policy. ₹1,65,000 is not small money, and relieving letter needs HR head's final signature which is delayed. Don't unnecessarily create tension over email!

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You clearly stated the exact total amount (₹1,65,000) and gave a firm timeline of 3 days.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: You mentioned 'employment laws' generally and threatened a labor commissioner. Make sure to ground your argument strictly in statutory provisions regarding timely wage payment and unauthorized withholding of dues without citing unsourced or restricted acts.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: My notice period ended on September 30, 2024, and assets were cleared; withholding earned wages and my relieving letter directly violates statutory wage provisions under the Code on Wages, 2019.
